clue.text: Sudden come-down for one on the mat

definitions.text: Sudden come-down for one on the mat

parts.words: Sudden come-down for one on the mat
parts.note: a fairground ride where you sit on a coir mat and whizz down a spiral chute, so the drop is quick and the rider is on a mat, not a gym floor

explanation.surface: A wrestler or gymnast is suddenly thrown down onto the mat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the mat' suggests wrestling or yoga, but the mat is the one riders sit on to slide down a tall spiral chute at a British fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground spiral slide is ridden on a mat and gives a quick descent.

clue.text: It inflames the frigid, that's the trouble with drink

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
to hit the bottle is to drink; bottle stands for drink

explanation.surface: Drinking is what warms up a cold person, and that is the problem with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflames the frigid' reads as passion, but it simply means warming someone cold in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber container of heated liquid taken to bed warms a chilly sleeper.

clue.text: Solicitor's withdrawal is obviously legal

indicators.note: a withdrawal is something drawn out, so letters are pulled from inside the word Solicitor's

explanation.surface: A lawyer pulling out of a case is plainly lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit is a formal synonym for lawful or permitted.

clue.text: A secretive arrangement to remove organs

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of a secretive are reordered

explanation.surface: A covert deal is struck for organ removal.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembowel is to take out the internal organs.

clue.text: Plain daughter walked slowly

parts.note: a steppe is a vast grassy plain

explanation.surface: An unattractive girl strolled along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the daughter, but it is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: To step is to walk with measured paces.

clue.text: City church in Cologne?

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A question about a church in the German city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne seems to be the German city, but it is eau de cologne, and the scented extract in it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume is made from a concentrated fragrant extract, which is found in cologne.

clue.text: Handsome orderly

definitions.meaning: considerable in amount, as a handsome profit

explanation.surface: A good-looking hospital attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome as in a sizeable sum, a tidy amount; and orderly as in neat.

clue.text: Manage a game of golf, say? Get an evasive reply

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a round is one game over the course

explanation.surface: Asking someone to organise a golf outing earns only a dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given the runaround means being fobbed off with excuses.

clue.text: Recreational area where coach gets sticky wickets?

parts.note: a hackney is a horse-drawn coach for hire
boggy ground; marshes are soggy, like a rain-sodden cricket pitch

explanation.surface: A sports ground where a cricket coach is faced with wet pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: HACKNEY MARSHES is a large expanse of public playing fields in east London; 'coach' and 'sticky wickets' read as cricket talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The London site is famous for its many Sunday football pitches, a public space for leisure.

clue.text: Miss Durbeyfield, taking in Bill and family, shows sticking power

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the name wraps the other pieces

parts.note: Tess Durbeyfield is the heroine of Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles
AC (account) is a bill
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Hardy's Tess, putting up a man called Bill and his relatives, proves she can persevere.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackiness is stickiness, the quality of adhering.

clue.text: Party girl turns into Spanish lady

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: turns means the girl's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl at a party is transformed into a Spanish señora.
explanation.definitionFit: Doña is the Spanish courtesy title for a woman, a lady.

clue.text: Mexican playing the part of Poirot, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the phrase and hear the sound it makes

parts.note: playing the part of is AS; Poirot is a detective, a TEC

explanation.surface: A Mexican actor cast as Agatha Christie's Belgian detective.
explanation.walkthrough: AS ('playing the part of') plus TEC (Poirot, a detective) is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people of the pre-Columbian empire in Mexico.

clue.text: Cut flower

definitions.meaning: to cut with ... shears, giving a zigzag edge
a dianthus, a clove-scented garden bloom

explanation.surface: A cut flower in a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: To pink is to cut cloth with a zigzag edge; a pink is also a garden carnation-like bloom.

clue.text: Chest holding a coarse spirit

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the chest goes round the letter

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A trunk containing a bottle of rough liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arak is a strong Middle Eastern liquor distilled from grapes or palm sap.

clue.text: Variety of night rates put in order

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of night rates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Several kinds of overnight tariff are tidied up.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten is to tidy or arrange neatly.

clue.text: When drunk, unending rudeness is guaranteed

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the remaining letters are jumbled
unending means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Being drunk is a sure route to endless rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' drops the last S of rudeness, leaving RUDENES, which 'When drunk' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ensured something is to have made it certain.

clue.text: Children's tablet, taken with iron perhaps, is saving society

parts.note: a slate was the writing tablet used by schoolchildren
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A child's writing slate, used with a flat-iron, is a thrifty association.
explanation.walkthrough: A SLATE CLUB is a British savings club whose members pay in weekly and share the fund out, often at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of such a club pool small regular sums, making it a thrift association.

clue.text: Former East-Ender, uneducated, is put out

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the ender of a word is its final letter, here taken from East

parts.note: rude in the old sense of untaught or unlearned

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered man who once lived in the East End is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East-Ender' looks like a Londoner from the East End; read as 'East' plus its ender, it gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to force or push something out.

clue.text: Blew up and swore

explanation.surface: Someone exploded with anger and cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasted is past tense of blast, both to blow up with explosives and to curse.

clue.text: Bad rule, unfortunately, is capable of lasting

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so bad rule is rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor regulation, regrettably, may stay in force a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable survives long use, it endures.

clue.text: Form of art in Gaelic festivals rejected in celebrities' world

indicators.note: in places the rearranged art inside the other piece
rejected means turned back, so the festivals are read in reverse

parts.note: a Mod is a Scottish Gaelic festival of music and poetry

indicators.note: form of means a new shape of the word art

explanation.surface: An art form at Highland cultural festivals is spurned in the world of the famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' turns art into TAR, which goes 'in' SDOM, MODS read backwards after 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the status and milieu of famous performers.

clue.text: Try to make an impression in demonstration side

parts.note: a show is a demonstration or display
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stand out at a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off is to flaunt oneself to impress others.

clue.text: Go on the wagon

parts.note: not giving up drink but travelling a long way by ox-wagon, as the Boer pioneers did

explanation.surface: Someone gives up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' is the idiom for abstaining, but here it is a literal ox-wagon journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, hard overland journey was originally a South African migration by ox-cart.

clue.text: Lines to a maiden showing vivacity

parts.note: BR is British Rail, whose railway lines are meant
Io was the maiden loved by Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A poem addressed to a young woman shows liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines to a maiden' reads as a love poem; lines are railway lines (BR) and the maiden is Io.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is spirited energy, as in con brio in music.

clue.text: In the king I have a patron

indicators.note: In places one piece inside the other

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Having the monarch on side means having a sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a donor, one who provides support.

clue.text: Anthony has no advertising numbers

indicators.note: has no means the surname is without the advertising letters

parts.note: Anthony Adverse is a 1933 historical novel by Hervey Allen, filmed in 1936
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A man called Anthony owns no adverts or figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anthony' stands for the title hero Anthony Adverse, whose surname less AD gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is an old word for poetry, metrical lines.

clue.text: End of the Rabbit's Tale for listeners

definitions.text: End of the Rabbit's Tale for listeners

parts.words: End of the Rabbit's Tale for listeners
parts.note: the end of a rabbit is its short tail, and a tale heard sounds like a tail

explanation.surface: The final part of a rabbit story being read to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'end' is not a story's ending but the rabbit's rear; tale and tail sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The short upright tail of a rabbit or deer has its own name.

clue.text: Light cloak was this colour for show

definitions.text: Light cloak was this colour for show

parts.words: Light cloak was this colour for show
parts.note: a domino is a light masquerade cloak, and the 1912 operetta The ___ Domino named its colour

explanation.surface: A light cape was dyed a certain shade for display.
explanation.walkthrough: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn at masked balls; 'show' is a stage show, the operetta The Lilac Domino.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale purple shade gave its name to the domino cloak of the operetta title.

clue.text: Fanlight concentrates the heat

parts.note: to fan is to blow air
a torch is a portable light

explanation.surface: A fanlight window focuses the warmth of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanlight' reads as the window over a door; split it into fan and light.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas tool used by plumbers directs an intense flame onto one spot.

clue.text: He is a dropper of fat members

parts.note: butter is a fat
fingers are members, parts of the body

explanation.surface: A man who keeps dropping things has greasy limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who keeps letting catches slip is so called.
